## Summary

Added `habit serve`:
- **`src/server.js`** — `renderPage(habits, today)` builds an HTML page listing each habit and its current streak (via the existing `currentStreak`), with HTML-escaping and an empty-state message; `serve(port)` starts a `node:http` server that reloads data from the store on every request.
- **`src/cli.js`** — wired up `serve` as a new subcommand (`habit serve [port]`, defaults to 3000).
- **`test/server.test.js`** — covers rendering a habit's streak, HTML-escaping, and the no-habits placeholder. All 10 tests pass (`npm test`).
- **`README.md`** — documented the new command.

I couldn't do a live end-to-end smoke test (curl against a running server) because background processes and network listeners require an approval prompt this sandboxed session can't answer — but the unit tests cover the rendering logic that the server relies on. Worth a quick `node src/cli.js serve` + browser check on your end before you consider it fully verified.
